To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
commodity risk is the result of the interplay of the following three economic forces: 1) supply-demand elasticity; 2) basis trading and arbitrage; 3) hedging response to risk.

1) E/CTRM system risk management functionality should be designed around a unified theory of commodity risk; 2) commodity risk is a function of supply and demand economics; 3) the hedging response is a function of the supply and demand economics of the commodity; 4) commodity risk is not a function of the price of the commodity; and 5) commodity risk can be managed using E/CTRM systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a theory that can unify the various theories of commodity risk, and in so doing, provide a more robust approach to risk management.
the development of a unifying theory for risk management within E/CTRM systems.
the development of an integrated commodity risk management system, and our discussion is intended to provide the theoretical framework for the development and evaluation of such a system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the E/CTRM systems are the most effective way to segment risk throughout the entire commodity supply chain, from production through consumption.
commodity hedging and arbitrage is an essential part of the risk management strategy for any commodity business.

the theory of commodity hedging and arbitrage can help unify the theory of risk management within E/CTRM systems, and in doing so, provide a framework to help solve the challenges associated with managing physical and financial supply chain risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
commodity hedging, as an economic tool for managing supply chain risk, is an effective means to achieve a desired level of risk tolerance and risk aversion.
E/CTRM systems should be designed to help manage risk, and not the other way around.

risk management systems must provide the ability to segment supply chain risk in order to provide a unified theory of commodity hedging and arbitrage.
